To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the event distribution of a decay chain with three invisible particle mass scales can be characterized by a single end point in the E1T-E2T plane, which can be used to extract the masses of the invisible particles.

(1) the event distribution in log(E1T /E2T) vs M12 plane can be used to extract the three invisible particle mass parameters in the decay chain of a two step decay chain with a missing particle at the end; (2) the mass measurement is sensitive to the mass hierarchy of invisible particle masses in this decay chain; (3) the mass measurement can be done in the absence of any information about the decay kinematics; (4) in many cases the mass
the invariant mass distribution of two visible particles in the decay of an invisible particle is not sufficient to determine the masses of all three invisible particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to measure the invisible particle masses in decay chains using a single end point.
the reconstruction of the invisible particle mass spectrum in the context of dark matter models.
the mass measurement of invisible particles in the context of the decay chains of dark matter candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three masses can be determined if the decay branching ratios of the two intermediate particles are known and can be determined if they are unknown.
, in general, the masses of three invisible particles in a decay chain of a single step can be measured with a single end point.
, with a single decay chain, the masses of the invisible particles in the chain can be determined, but the accuracy of the mass measurement would be model dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with a single short decay, the invisible particle masses can be extracted from a single invariant mass end point with the log(E1t/E2t) distribution.
, for the decay chain of two invisible particles and a single visible particle, the three invisible particle mass measurements can be done in the log(ET1/ET2) vs. invariant-mass-squared plane.

the invisible particles in the two-step decay chains can be individually measured with high accuracy if the two visible particles in the chain are well separated, and the mass measurement becomes challenging when the two visible particles are close to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the invariant mass of the two visible final states in a decay chain is not the only information that can be extracted from the data.
a careful analysis can extract more information than is naively expected.
, for many models, the mass measurements of the invisible particles are possible with a single decay chain.
